info.title: IdentityControlService
info.description:
Control API for IRIS API-key lifecycle and grant management.

Callers authenticate with the Identity Service's static control credential (the
deployment admin) or, when configured, an operator JWT (auth.oidc or auth.sm_cloud).
Credential and grant operations are authorized per product. Callers other than
the deployment admin are confined to their own tenant, and another tenant's key is reported as not found.
The raw API-key token is returned only on create and rotate.

get.description:
Lists the products configured in product_validation and their supported API-key
grant actions, grouped by resource type. Every authenticated Control caller may
read this catalog; it does not describe the caller's authority to issue grants.
Products, resource types and actions are sorted lexically. A configured product
without registered grantable resource types has an empty resourceTypes array.

post.description:
Finds or creates the grant set of one subject in one tenant and returns its ID.
The response is 201 when the set is new and 200 when it already exists, so a
retry is safe. Grants that were stored before their set existed get a set the
first time that a caller asks for it. While a delete of the subject's set
runs, the response is 503. Retry after the delete.

200.description: CreateSubjectGrantSet 200 response: the set already exists

put.description:
Grants attached directly to an externally authenticated subject, identified by
its token issuer and a user ID taken from that token. The Identity Service never
sees that token: the data plane validates it locally and asks only for the
subject's grants.

A grant is addressed by (issuer, subject, tenant, product, resourceType,
resourceId). Putting the same address again replaces its actions. Grants must name
an exact tenant and resource; wildcard resources and constraints are rejected.

post.description:
Changes the grants of one product of a subject in one call. First the Identity
Service finds or creates the set of (tenant, issuer, subject), as
CreateSubjectGrantSet does. Then it applies the grants as
PatchProductSubjectGrants does, with the same Merge Patch semantics and
managementId rules. A null entry removes a grant,
so this call also revokes. A 409 means an ownership conflict. If a delete of
the set runs at the same time, the response is 503 and a retry gets a new set.

parameters.name: managementId
parameters.description: Optional controller ownership for each entry.

schema.description: Optional controller ownership for each entry.

patch.description:
Changes the grants of one product with JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) semantics.
Send application/merge-patch+json or application/json. An entry with actions
adds the grant or replaces its actions. A null entry removes the grant. Entries
that the patch does not name do not change. The Identity Service applies all
entries in one atomic write, or it applies none of them.

With managementId, the request acts as that controller. It reconciles only its
own grants, borrows an adequate unowned grant without changing it, and retires
the identifier at each address that it removes, so a delayed retry cannot add
the grant again. A conflict returns 409.

With If-Match, the patch applies only when the product's version is still the
given ETag. Otherwise the response is 412.

parameters.description: A grant set ID: a random UUID as 32 lowercase hex characters.

post.description:
Adds the record of an external IdP to a tenant (MOD-19954). If the tenant
already has a record with this name, IdS changes nothing and returns 409. Only
the deployment admin can call it.

The token exchange and the product resolver read the records. A record has the
rules of a configured OIDC issuer: an https issuer and jwksUri, and no none or
symmetric algorithm. The audience is one value without a wildcard. IdS refuses
an http issuer in a record, also for AD FS; such an IdP needs the static
auth.oidc configuration.

With tokenExchange, the token exchange accepts the tokens of the IdP for the
tenant (MOD-19927). The settings have the rules of a configured JWT entry. A
record whose matchers can match the same token as another record of any
tenant, or as a configured entry, returns 409.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: A tenant identifier as in TenantId, without "/" and without a space at its ends, and not "." or "..", because the tenant is a part of the path.

schema.description: A tenant identifier as in TenantId, without "/" and without a space at its ends, and not "." or "..", because the tenant is a part of the path.

put.description:
Replaces all the external IdP records of a tenant with the records in the
body. IdS removes each record that is not in the body, so an empty list removes
all the records. Two records must not have the same name. IdS stores all the
records or none. Only the deployment admin can call it. A record whose
tokenExchange matchers can match the same token as another record returns 409.

With expectedRevision, IdS replaces the records only if the revision of all
the records of the tenant is still this value. Otherwise the answer is 412
with the type /errors/revision-conflict.

grants.description:
Grants where an empty list is not a meaningful answer. On create and update, an
explicitly supplied but empty list is a caller mistake rather than a request to
clear grants. On API-key introspection, reporting an active key with no grants
would read to a data plane as an authenticated caller with no authorization, so
the response must either carry grants or fail.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds after which the key no longer authenticates; 0 or omitted means never.

userId.description: The user that the key acts as. Optional: a key without a user acts as no user. It cannot change after the mint. Requires API key user binding to be enabled in the deployment. The deployment admin and an on-prem suite_admin can set any user; another caller can set only its own user ID.

issuer.description: The token issuer of the subject. Omit it to use the issuer of the caller's own token. A caller without a token issuer, such as the Control credential, must send it.

subject.description: The subject's user ID, taken from its token. Long enough for any Kubernetes ServiceAccount subject: system:serviceaccount: plus a 63-character namespace and a 253-character name.

title.description:
A short, human-readable summary of the problem
                                      type.  It SHOULD NOT change from occurrence to occurrence of the
                                      problem, except for purposes of localization (e.g., using
                                      proactive content negotiation; see [RFC7231], Section 3.4).

status.description: The HTTP status code ([RFC7231], Section 6) generated by the origin server for this occurrence of the problem.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem.

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of the problem.  It may or may not yield further information if dereferenced.

managementId.description: The controller that owns the grant. Absent when no controller owns it.

id.description: A grant set ID: a random UUID as 32 lowercase hex characters.

tenant.description: An opaque tenant identifier, for example a Redis Cloud account ID or account URN. It must not contain "|" or control characters.

subject.description: The subject's user ID, taken from its token. Long enough for any Kubernetes ServiceAccount subject: system:serviceaccount: plus a 63-character namespace and a 253-character name.

TenantProperties.description:
Non-secret JSON properties. Keys use namespaces such as memory.ownership.enabled.
At most 256 properties and 64 KiB of JSON. An empty map clears the overlay.

TokenExchangeGrantMode.description:
How the token exchange gives grants to the subjects of the IdP. The
token_exchange configuration names this mode subject_grants. A record holds
only trust, and no grants, so it has no issuer_grants mode. The member stays,
so that a later mode is not a breaking change.

UnexpectedErrorType.description: Problem type URI for unexpected internal errors.

grants.description:
Grants where an empty list is not a meaningful answer. On create and update, an
explicitly supplied but empty list is a caller mistake rather than a request to
clear grants. On API-key introspection, reporting an active key with no grants
would read to a data plane as an authenticated caller with no authorization, so
the response must either carry grants or fail.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds after which the key no longer authenticates; 0 clears expiry.

tenantId.description: Immutable tenant that owns this key, independently of its grants.

grants.description:
Grants as returned by the Control read models. Unconstrained: a key may be
created with no grants, and such a key encodes an empty array.

userId.description:
The user that the key acts as, when the mint set one. A key created
before the current user ID rules can return a user ID that does not follow them.
